parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the effect of the colour of the outside surface of a beaker on the rate of cooling of water in the beaker. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 2.1. Beaker A is covered with thin black card. Beaker B is covered with shiny metal foil.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Remove the lid from beaker A. Pour 150 cm 3 of hot water into beaker A and replace the lid. Place the thermometer in the water. In the first row of Table 2.1, record the temperature θ of the water at time t = 0 and immediately start the stop-clock. Record the temperature θ of the water at t = 30 s, t = 60 s, t = 90 s, t = 120 s, t = 150 s and t = 180 s. Remove the thermometer from the beaker. [1]

ms.label: 2(b)(i)
ms.text:
θ for beaker B decreasing and all temperatures recorded to at least 1°C
θ for beaker B decreasing less quickly than beaker A

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Add units to the column headings in Table 2.1. [1]

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text:
statement matching readings in table
comparison of temperature changes over 180 s, matching statement (need to see values used in justification)

parts.label: i
parts.text: (d) (i) Calculate the average cooling rate x A for the water in beaker A during the experiment. Use your readings for beaker A from Table 2.1 and the equation x A = θ 0 – θ 180 T where T = 180 s and θ 0 and θ 180 are the temperatures of the water in beaker A at times t = 0 and t = 180 s. Include the unit for the cooling rate. x A = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the average cooling rate x B for the water in beaker B during the experiment. Use your readings for beaker B from Table 2.1 and the equation x B = θ 0 – θ 180 T where T = 180 s and θ 0 and θ 180 are the temperatures of the water in beaker B at times t = 0 and t = 180 s. Include the unit. x B = ......................................................... [1]
